mn135:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
mn135:2.1: Then the student Subha, Todeyya’s son, went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
mn135:2.2: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. When he had done so, the student Subha, Todeyya’s son, said to the Blessed One:
mn135:3.1: ‘Master Gotama, what is the reason, what is the condition, why inferiority and superiority are met with among human beings, among mankind?
mn135:3.2: For, Master Gotama, one meets with short-lived men, one meets with long-lived men;
mn135:3.3: one meets with sickly men, one meets with healthy men;
mn135:3.4: one meets with ugly men, one meets with beautiful men;
mn135:3.5: one meets with insignificant men, one meets with influential men;
mn135:3.6: one meets with poor men, one meets with rich men;
mn135:3.7: one meets with low-born men, one meets with high-born men;
mn135:3.8: one meets with stupid men, one meets with wise men.
mn135:3.9: What is the reason, Master Gotama, what is the condition, why inferiority and superiority are met with among human beings, among mankind?’
mn135:4.1: ‘Student, beings are owners of kammas, heirs of kammas, they have kammas as their progenitor, kammas as their kin, kammas as their homing-place.
mn135:4.2: It is kammas that differentiate beings, that is to say,
mn135:4.4: ‘I do not understand the detailed meaning of Master Gotama’s utterance, spoken in brief without expounding the detailed meaning.
mn135:4.5: It would be good if Master Gotama taught me the Dhamma so that I might understand the detailed meaning of Master Gotama’s utterance, spoken in brief without expounding the detailed meaning.’
mn135:4.6: ‘Then, student, listen and heed well what I shall say.’
mn135:4.7: ‘Yes, sir,’ the student Subha, Todeyya’s son, replied to the Blessed One.
mn135:5.1: ‘Here, student, some woman or man is a killer of living beings, murderous, bloody-handed, given to blows and violence, merciless to all living beings.
mn135:5.2: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn135:5.3: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is short-lived wherever he is reborn.
mn135:5.4: This, student, is the way that leads to a short life, that is to say,
mn135:5.5: to be a killer of living beings, murderous, bloody-handed, given to blows and violence, merciless to all living beings.
mn135:6.1: ‘But here, student, some woman or man, having abandoned the killing of living beings, abstains from killing living beings; with rod and knife laid aside, conscientious and merciful, he abides compassionate for the welfare of all living beings.
mn135:6.2: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.
mn135:6.3: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is long-lived wherever he is reborn.
mn135:6.4: This, student, is the way that leads to a long life, that is to say,
mn135:6.5: having abandoned the killing of living beings, to abstain from killing living beings; with rod and knife laid aside, conscientious and merciful, to abide compassionate for the welfare of all living beings.
mn135:7.1: ‘Here, student, some woman or man is given to persecuting beings with the hand, or with a clod, or with a stick, or with a knife.
mn135:7.2: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn135:7.3: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is sickly wherever he is reborn.
mn135:7.4: This, student, is the way that leads to sickliness, that is to say,
mn135:7.5: to be given to persecuting beings with the hand, or with a clod, or with a stick, or with a knife.
mn135:8.1: ‘But here, student, some woman or man is not given to persecuting beings with the hand, or with a clod, or with a stick, or with a knife.
mn135:8.2: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.
mn135:8.3: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is healthy wherever he is reborn.
mn135:8.4: This, student, is the way that leads to health, that is to say,
mn135:8.5: not to be given to persecuting beings with the hand, or with a clod, or with a stick, or with a knife.
mn135:9.1: ‘Here, student, some woman or man is angry and much given to rage.
mn135:9.2: Even when little is said, he is furious, angered, ill-disposed, resentful, and he shows ill-temper, hatred, and bitterness.
mn135:9.3: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn135:9.4: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is ugly wherever he is reborn.
mn135:9.5: This, student, is the way that leads to ugliness, that is to say,
mn135:9.6: to be angry and much given to rage;
mn135:9.7: even when little is said, to be furious, angered, ill-disposed, resentful, and to show ill-temper, hatred, and bitterness.
mn135:10.1: ‘But here, student, some woman or man is not angry, nor much given to rage;
mn135:10.2: even when much is said, he is not furious, angered, ill-disposed, resentful, nor does he show ill-temper, hatred, and bitterness.
mn135:10.3: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.
mn135:10.4: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is beautiful wherever he is reborn.
mn135:10.5: This, student, is the way that leads to beauty, that is to say,
mn135:10.6: not to be angry, nor much given to rage;
mn135:10.7: even when much is said, not to be furious, angered, ill-disposed, resentful, nor to show ill-temper, hatred, and bitterness.
mn135:11.1: ‘Here, student, some woman or man has an envious nature;
mn135:11.2: he envies, begrudges, and harbours envy about others’ gains, honour, veneration, respect, salutations, and offerings.
mn135:11.3: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn135:11.4: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is insignificant wherever he is reborn.
mn135:11.5: This, student, is the way that leads to insignificance, that is to say,
mn135:11.7: to envy, begrudge, and harbour envy about others’ gains, honour, veneration, respect, salutations, and offerings.
mn135:12.1: ‘But here, student, some woman or man does not have an envious nature;
mn135:12.2: he does not envy, begrudge, or harbour envy about others’ gains, honour, veneration, respect, salutations, and offerings.
mn135:12.3: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.
mn135:12.4: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is influential wherever he is reborn.
mn135:12.5: This, student, is the way that leads to influence, that is to say,
mn135:12.6: not to have an envious nature;
mn135:12.7: not to envy, begrudge, or harbour envy about others’ gains, honour, veneration, respect, salutations, and offerings.
mn135:13.1: ‘Here, student, some woman or man is not a giver of food, drink, clothing, a vehicle, garlands, scent, unguent, bedding, dwelling, and lighting to ascetics or brahmins.
mn135:13.2: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn135:13.3: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is poor wherever he is reborn.
mn135:13.4: This, student, is the way that leads to poverty, that is to say,
mn135:13.5: not to be a giver of food, drink, clothing, a vehicle, garlands, scent, unguent, bedding, dwelling, and lighting to ascetics or brahmins.
mn135:14.1: ‘But here, student, some woman or man is a giver of food, drink, clothing, a vehicle, garlands, scent, unguent, bedding, dwelling, and lighting to ascetics or brahmins.
mn135:14.2: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.
mn135:14.3: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is rich wherever he is reborn.
mn135:14.4: This, student, is the way that leads to riches, that is to say,
mn135:14.5: to be a giver of food, drink, clothing, a vehicle, garlands, scent, unguent, bedding, dwelling, and lighting to ascetics or brahmins.
mn135:15.1: ‘Here, student, some woman or man is obstinate and arrogant—
mn135:15.2: he does not pay homage to one who should be paid homage, does not rise up for one for whom he should rise up, does not give a seat to one who deserves a seat, does not make way for one for whom he should make way, does not honour one who should be honoured, does not respect one who should be respected, does not esteem one who should be esteemed, does not revere one who should be revered.
mn135:15.3: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn135:15.4: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is low-born wherever he is reborn.
mn135:15.5: This, student, is the way that leads to low birth, that is to say,
mn135:15.7: not to pay homage to one who should be paid homage, not to rise up for one for whom he should rise up, not to give a seat to one who deserves a seat, not to make way for one for whom he should make way, not to honour one who should be honoured, not to respect one who should be respected, not to esteem one who should be esteemed, not to revere one who should be revered.
mn135:16.1: ‘But here, student, some woman or man is not obstinate, nor arrogant;
mn135:16.2: he pays homage to one who should be paid homage, rises up for one for whom he should rise up, gives a seat to one who deserves a seat, makes way for one for whom he should make way, honours one who should be honoured, respects one who should be respected, esteems one who should be esteemed, reveres one who should be revered.
mn135:16.3: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.
mn135:16.4: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is high-born wherever he is reborn.
mn135:16.5: This, student, is the way that leads to high birth, that is to say,
mn135:16.6: not to be obstinate, nor arrogant;
mn135:16.7: to pay homage to one who should be paid homage, to rise up for one for whom he should rise up, to give a seat to one who deserves a seat, to make way for one for whom he should make way, to honour one who should be honoured, to respect one who should be respected, to esteem one who should be esteemed, to revere one who should be revered.
mn135:17.1: ‘Here, student, some woman or man, on visiting an ascetic or a brahmin, does not ask:
mn135:17.2: “What, venerable sir, is profitable, what is unprofitable;
mn135:17.3: what is blamable, what is blameless;
mn135:17.4: what should be cultivated, what should not be cultivated;
mn135:17.5: what, by my doing it, will be for my harm and suffering for a long time, or what, by my doing it, will be for my welfare and happiness for a long time?”
mn135:17.6: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell.
mn135:17.7: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a state of deprivation, in an unhappy destination, in perdition, in hell, he comes to the human state, he is stupid wherever he is reborn.
mn135:17.8: This, student, is the way that leads to stupidity, that is to say,
mn135:17.9: on visiting an ascetic or a brahmin, not to ask:
mn135:17.10: “What, venerable sir, is profitable, what is unprofitable;
mn135:17.11: what is blamable, what is blameless;
mn135:17.12: what should be cultivated, what should not be cultivated;
mn135:17.13: what, by my doing it, will be for my harm and suffering for a long time, or what, by my doing it, will be for my welfare and happiness for a long time?”
mn135:18.1: ‘But here, student, some woman or man, on visiting an ascetic or a brahmin, asks:
mn135:18.2: “What, venerable sir, is profitable, what is unprofitable;
mn135:18.3: what is blamable, what is blameless;
mn135:18.4: what should be cultivated, what should not be cultivated;
mn135:18.5: what, by my doing it, will be for my harm and suffering for a long time, or what, by my doing it, will be for my welfare and happiness for a long time?”
mn135:18.6: Due to having performed and completed such kamma, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in the heavenly world.
mn135:18.7: If, on the dissolution of the body, after death, instead of reappearing in a happy destination, in the heavenly world, he comes to the human state, he is wise wherever he is reborn.
mn135:18.8: This, student, is the way that leads to wisdom, that is to say,
mn135:18.9: on visiting an ascetic or a brahmin, to ask:
mn135:18.10: “What, venerable sir, is profitable, what is unprofitable;
mn135:18.11: what is blamable, what is blameless;
mn135:18.12: what should be cultivated, what should not be cultivated;
mn135:18.13: what, by my doing it, will be for my harm and suffering for a long time, or what, by my doing it, will be for my welfare and happiness for a long time?”
mn135:19.1: ‘So, student, the way that leads to a short life makes men short-lived, the way that leads to a long life makes men long-lived;
mn135:19.2: the way that leads to sickliness makes men sickly, the way that leads to health makes men healthy;
mn135:19.3: the way that leads to ugliness makes men ugly, the way that leads to beauty makes men beautiful;
mn135:19.4: the way that leads to insignificance makes men insignificant, the way that leads to influence makes men influential;
mn135:19.5: the way that leads to poverty makes men poor, the way that leads to riches makes men rich;
mn135:19.6: the way that leads to low birth makes men low-born, the way that leads to high birth makes men high-born;
mn135:19.7: the way that leads to stupidity makes men stupid, the way that leads to wisdom makes men wise.
mn135:20.1: ‘Beings, student, are owners of kammas, heirs of kammas, they have kammas as their progenitor, kammas as their kin, kammas as their homing-place.
mn135:20.2: It is kammas that differentiate beings, that is to say,
mn135:21.1: When this was said, the student Subha, Todeyya’s son, said to the Blessed One:
mn135:21.3: Master Gotama has made the Dhamma clear in many ways, as though he were turning upright what had been overthrown, revealing what was hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, or holding up a lamp in the dark for those with eyes to see forms.
mn135:21.4: I go to Master Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
mn135:21.5: From today let Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone to him for refuge for life.’
